Class Abilities

1st Level

Spell Use

  • Effect: Cast arcane folk-magic spells, learned from a patron, per the Spells Per Day table.
  • You prepare spells each morning from the whole Witch list (see Spellcasting in Arneyan).
  • Bonus slots from high Wisdom (see Spellcasting in Arneyan, II).
  • A Witch comes to each new level of spells later than a Wizard or Cleric does: her Hex and her cauldron carry the years between.

Familiar

  • Effect: Bond a small animal familiar in keeping with your Patron (a black cat, a raven, a toad, a moth: GM and player agree on the creature).
  • The familiar has 1 HP per two Witch levels (minimum 1), AC 14, and can deliver a Hex or touch spell on your behalf as your action if it is within 60ft of you and adjacent to the target.
  • You make any touch attack.
  • If the familiar dies, it can be re-bonded after a long rest and a small personal cost the GM determines
  • The familiar can speak a handful of simple words and understands your intent even at a distance within 1 mile
  • At-will, no action cost from you: the familiar acts on its own each round — it can move, scout, hide, or carry small objects independently, sharing what it sees or hears with you at any distance within 1 mile.
  • 6th: Your familiar has 1 HP per Witch level and AC 16.

Hag's Vigour

  • Effect: Your patron's old magic runs truer in you: you're hardier than your spindly d6 Hit Die suggests. Gain a permanent +1 bonus to maximum HP per Witch level: in effect a d8 Hit Die.
  • 8th: +2 maximum HP per Witch level instead: in effect a d10 Hit Die. Beyond 10th level the Vigour adds +1 a level, so you gain 3 HP a level plus your Constitution modifier, as a d10 class does.

Hex (Wisdom)

  • Effect: As an action, curse one creature within 30ft: Will save or have Disadvantage on one of: attack rolls, saving throws of one kind (Fortitude, Reflex or Will), or attribute checks (your choice when you cast it) for the encounter.
  • While hexed, it also takes 1d6 necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns (2d6 at 5th, 3d6 at 9th, 4d6 at 13th, 5d6 at 17th), and repeats the Will save at the end of each of its turns, ending the Hex on a success.
  • The Disadvantage never applies to saves against the Hex itself.
  • You can Hex at will.
  • You can have only one Hex active; a new Hex ends the old one.
  • Remove Curse ends a Hex.

Cauldron Brews

  • Effect: During a long rest, brew draughts in your cauldron (a pot, kettle or skull will do). You brew 2 draughts at 1st level, 3 at 5th, 4 at 9th, 5 at 13th and 6 at 17th.
  • A draught keeps its power until your next long rest.
  • Drinking a draught takes no action of its own: you do it as part of your action, one draught a round.
  • Pouring one into a willing or helpless creature, or throwing a splash brew up to 20ft, works the same way.
  • Anyone may drink; effects use your Witch level and Class Save DC.
  • You know 4 recipes at 1st level, and learn 2 more at 5th, 9th, 13th and 17th (see Cauldron Recipes).
  • Each recipe improves at 5th, 9th, 13th and 17th. Each tier adds to the one before unless it says otherwise.

Patron's Recipe

  • Effect: You know your Patron's recipe (see Patrons) from 1st level beyond your four, and brew one extra draught of it each long rest. If you would learn it again, choose another recipe.

2nd Level

Passing Hex

  • Effect: When a creature under your Hex drops to 0 HP, you may at once pass its share of the Hex to another creature you can see within the Hex's range. It saves as normal, and your other hexed creatures are unaffected. This needs no action.

3rd Level

Patron Boon (Curse)

  • Effect: Gain the Curse granted by your Patron. A Curse takes your action and uses your Class Save DC unless it says otherwise, but you may lay it as part of the action you use to Hex the same creature; it saves against each separately.

5th Level

Twin Hex

  • Effect: When you Hex, you may name a second creature within the Hex's range. All take the Disadvantage you chose; each saves on its own, and one shaking it off leaves it on the others.
  • 17th: You may name a third creature.

7th Level

Patron Boon (Physical Change)

  • Effect: Gain the Physical Change granted by your Patron. It is permanent and visible, and gives you a natural weapon (claws unless your Patron says otherwise; 1d6, lethal).
  • Its once-a-day power spends your Curse for the day: each day you lay the Curse or use the power, not both (both from 18th). It takes your action and uses your Class Save DC unless it says otherwise.

10th Level

Far Hex

  • Effect: Your Hex reaches 60ft, and your familiar can deliver it to a creature within 30ft of itself.

15th Level

  • Patron's Recipe improves: you brew a second extra draught of it each long rest.
  • Wisdom Bonus: permanent +1 Wisdom. It can take the score past 20, to 22 at most (see The Mortal Limit in Character Creation).

18th Level

  • Patron Boon (Curse) improves: usable twice per day, and the target makes its save with Disadvantage. You may now use your Physical Change's daily power as well.

20th Level

Cauldron of the Ninth Moon

  • Effect: On a night the GM names (a moon or a turning of the season, about once a season), you may brew the Ninth Moon: one effect of Wish cast as a Ritual (see Wish in Spellcasting in Arneyan), with no Exhaustion and for half the cost of its components. Anything beyond that list needs the GM's leave, and the Cauldron then leaves a mark on you.

Renown: Coven

  • Effect: You may gather a coven (see Renown in The Arneyan Codex); each season 1d4 hedge-witches (1st level) join it. While you hold it, you brew one extra draught each long rest.

24th Level

Scapegoat

  • Effect: Once per encounter, when you or an ally you can see within 60ft would take damage, you may pass it to a creature under your Hex.
  • It makes a Will save: on a failure it takes the damage instead; on a success the damage falls where it was aimed.
  • This needs no action.
  • Cauldron of the Ninth Moon improves: once a month, on any night.
  • Hex improves: a creature makes its first save against your Hex with Disadvantage.

Cauldron Recipes

  • Each recipe lists its 1st-level effect, then what it adds at 5th, 9th, 13th and 17th. Choose your known recipes from this list.
  • Witch Bottle: Advantage on saves of one kind (Fortitude, Reflex or Will, the drinker's choice) for an hour. 5th: Also ends curses laid by a spell of 3rd level or lower, and one disease. 9th: Advantage on a second kind of save, and temporary HP equal to your Witch level + Wisdom modifier. 13th: Also can't be Frightened or Charmed for the hour. 17th: Advantage on all three kinds; also ends any curse; the temporary HP doubles.
  • Seer's Draught: An omen about a place or person. 5th: One yes-or-no answer. 9th: A short vision. 13th: One question answered truthfully in a sentence. 17th: Also can't be surprised for a day.
  • Threshold Salt (poured on a doorway): Until your next long rest, you know when anything crosses it. 5th: A hostile spirit or fey of Level up to your Witch level can't cross; a stronger one crosses on a Will save. 9th: Covers a whole building. 13th: Undead and fiends likewise. 17th: Covers a castle or a village quarter, and you name one further kind of creature.
  • Familiar's Broth (fed to the familiar): Your familiar ranges up to 5 miles and can carry a message there and back. 5th: 20 miles. 9th: You can cast a spell with a range of Touch through it at that distance. 13th: Anywhere on the same plane you have been. 17th: It can cross into the Feywild or the Shadowfell and back.
  • Hag's Remedy: A dying creature wakes at 1 HP, and Poisoned ends. 5th: Also ends one disease. 9th: Also restores 2d8 HP. 13th: Restores 4d8 HP and ends Paralysed or Petrified. 17th: Restores 6d8 HP; a creature that died within the last round returns at 1 HP if its soul is willing, with 2 levels of Exhaustion.
  • Nightsight Tea: Darkvision 60ft for an hour. 5th: Sees through magical darkness. 9th: Sees Invisible creatures for one encounter. 13th: Sees as True Seeing out to 30ft for one encounter. 17th: Sees as True Seeing out to 60ft for an hour.
  • Hearthfire Broth: Temporary HP 1d8 + your Witch level, for an hour. 5th: 2d8 + level. 9th: 3d8 + level. 13th: 4d8 + level, and Resistance 5 to cold and fire. 17th: 5d8 + level, and immune to cold.
  • Hex Oil (on a weapon): For the encounter, one hit of the wielder's choice each round deals +1d6 necrotic; this is that hit's rider. 5th: +2d6. 9th: The target also can't regain HP until the end of its next turn. 13th: +3d6. 17th: +4d6; a creature it kills can't be raised by anything less than Wish.
  • Murk Brew (splash): A 10ft cloud of fog (heavily obscured) for the encounter. 5th: 20ft, and a creature that enters the cloud or starts its turn there makes a Fortitude save or is Poisoned until it leaves. 9th: You and your allies see through it. 13th: 30ft; a Poisoned creature inside takes 2d6 poison damage at the start of its turn. 17th: You can move the cloud 20ft each round as part of your action.
  • Toad's Leap: Triple jump distance and no damage from falls, for an hour. 5th: Also climb walls as if they were floors. 9th: A fly speed of 30ft for 10 minutes. 13th: A fly speed of 60ft for an hour. 17th: Also can't be Grappled or Restrained.
  • Silver Tongue Syrup: The drinker's lies can't be detected by magic for an hour. 5th: Also speaks and understands any language. 9th: One creature that talks with them is Charmed by them (Will negates). 13th: Once, a one-sentence suggestion the creature follows (Will negates). 17th: Everyone listening is Charmed by them for the encounter (Will negates).
  • Grave Dust Tea: Ask a corpse one question. 5th: Three questions. 9th: See its last memory. 13th: Talk with the dead for 10 minutes as if alive. 17th: The spirit answers even if only dust or bones remain, however old.
  • Sleepwell Draught: The drinker's next rest outdoors heals as a night in a safe haven. 5th: Also removes one level of Exhaustion. 9th: Regain HP as for two nights' rest. 13th: Also removes all Exhaustion. 17th: One hour of sleep counts as a long rest (still once per 24 hours).
  • Beast Tongue: Speak with animals for an hour. 5th: Animals start friendly towards the drinker. 9th: Call a local beast of Level up to half your Witch level to help for an hour. 13th: The beast can be up to two-thirds your Witch level. 17th: Up to your Witch level, or a swarm of lesser beasts, for the encounter, or for a day as a guide and mount that will not fight. You can have only one called beast at a time, and it counts as your one summoned attacker (see Summoned and conjured attackers in Spellcasting in Arneyan); calling another sends the first home.

Witch Spells Per Day

  • The Witch draws from her own folk-magic spell list: mostly Wizard spells of the Enchantment, Necromancy and Divination schools, with Cleric and Druid spells beside them. Bonus spells from high Wisdom apply once the Witch is high enough level to cast that tier.

Witch Spell List

Spells available to the Witch, by level. * = reversible spell. ‡ = needs a costed material component (see Rare Spell Components in the Shopkeeper's Catalogue).

  • Full descriptions, saves and components are in Spellcasting in Arneyan.
  • Spells marked in the Class-Only list below exist for this class alone.
  • Includes every Wizard-list spell of the Witch’s favoured schools (Enchantment, Necromancy and Divination), up to the highest spell level the Witch can cast, except Power Word Stun, Power Word Blind and Power Word Kill.

0 Level (Cantrips)

Detect Magic · Detect Poison · First Aid · Ghost Sound · Know Direction · Light · Mending · Purify Food and Drink · Read Magic · Resistance · Toll the Dead

1st Level

Bless* · Charm Person · Chill Touch · Comprehend Languages · Cure Light Wounds* · Entangle · Faerie Fire · Friends · Identify‡ · Mage Armour · Protection from Alignment · Sleep

2nd Level

Augury‡ · Barkskin · Blindness/Deafness · Detect Thoughts* · Hold Person · Invisibility · Locate Object* · Obscuring Mist · Ray of Enfeeblement · See Invisibility · Silence · Speak with Animals · Speak with Dead · Tasha's Hideous Laughter · Web

3rd Level

Animate Dead*‡ · Bestow Curse · Clairaudience/Clairvoyance · Cure Serious Wounds* · Dispel Magic · Remove Curse* · Speak with Plants · Suggestion · Tongues* · Vampiric Touch

Arcane Eye · Blight · Charm Monster · Confusion · Detect Scrying · Divination‡ · Fear · Freedom of Movement · Locate Creature · Neutralise Poison · Polymorph · Reincarnate‡ · Restoration*‡ · Scrying‡

Class-Only Spells

Ill Omen (Cantrip; Necromancy; V, S) — Range 30ft; one creature has Disadvantage on its next attribute check (not an attack roll or saving throw) within the hour; Will negates.

Hex of Stumbling (1st; Transmutation; V, S) — Range 30ft; one creature's speed is halved for 1 minute; Reflex negates.

Bind Wound (2nd; Necromancy; V, S, M) — Touch; heals 1d8 HP plus 1 per level (max +10).

Evil Eye (2nd; Enchantment; V, S) — Range 30ft; one creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls for the encounter; Will negates, with no repeat save.

Contagion (3rd; Necromancy; V, S) — Touch; one creature catches a disease of your choice (see Disease & Poison in The Arneyan Codex), with effects starting at once (touch attack); it makes the disease's save against your spell DC.

Withering Glance (3rd; Necromancy; V, S) — Range 30ft; one creature ages 1d4 years (the ageing is permanent) and has −1 Strength and Constitution for 1 day; Fortitude negates.

Wither Limb (4th; Necromancy; V, S) — Range 30ft; one limb of a creature is useless for 1 day per level (an arm drops what it holds; a leg halves speed); Fortitude negates. Remove Curse or Restoration ends it.

Withering Curse (8th; Necromancy; V, S, M) — Range 30ft; one creature takes 1 Constitution damage at the start of each of its turns; Fortitude negates, and it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on a success.

  • Remove Curse also ends it.
  • Lost Constitution returns at 1 point per long rest once the curse ends.

Patrons

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Witch folder. Drag one onto your character.

  • Choose one Patron at character creation. Your Patron defines your Patron's recipe (1st), Curse (3rd) and Physical Change (7th). Five of Arneyan's classic hag types are represented here, alongside the folkloric Baba Yaga and two wholly original Arneyan patrons.
  • Patron — Vashtira, the Widow of Dreams (Night Hag)
  • She walks the space between sleep and waking, riding the dreams of the exhausted and collecting what they'd rather forget. Her Witches wake tired for reasons they can't explain, carrying a little less of themselves than they went to bed with.
  • Recipe (1st): Witch Bottle.
  • Curse (3rd): Once per day, afflict a creature within 30ft with Vashtira's Weight (Will save against your Class Save DC): while cursed, the target's dreams are haunted and it gains no benefit from rest until Remove Curse ends it or a week passes.
  • Physical Change (7th): Your eyes lose their whites: solid black, cold to look into.
  • You gain darkvision and Advantage on saves against being magically put to sleep.
  • Once per day, without spending your action, lock your gaze on a creature within 30ft: Will save or Frightened of you until the end of its next turn.
  • Patron — Old Mossmaw of the Nalwood Deep (Green Hag)
  • Every swamp has one, or claims to. Old Mossmaw wears a different lovely face every time she's seen, and every villager who's traded with her swears they got the better deal — until they check what they actually walked away with.
  • Recipe (1st): Silver Tongue Syrup.
  • Curse (3rd): Once per day, force a creature within 30ft to see themselves as hideous in every reflective surface for 24 hours (Will save negates) — Disadvantage on Charisma checks with anyone who has seen their reflection.
  • Physical Change (7th): Your skin takes on a faint mottled green cast in dim light, and warts bloom at your knuckles.
  • Advantage on Stealth checks when you are in mud, water or thick growth.
  • Your hands harden with a bog-witch's grip: your natural weapon is your fists, and you have Advantage on grapple and overbearing checks.
  • Patron — Grigsdotter Ironjaw (Annis Hag)
  • A hill-den brute with a grip that's cracked stone and a temper to match. Grigsdotter doesn't bargain in riddles like the others — she bargains in favours owed and debts collected, and she always collects.
  • Recipe (1st): Hex Oil.
  • Curse (3rd): Once per day, when a creature fails its save against your Hex, the Hex deals an extra 2d6 damage the first time it harms that creature (4d6 from 13th). This needs no action.
  • Physical Change (7th): Your nails thicken into short, blackened claws, and you have Advantage on Strength checks to break or force objects. Your claw deals an extra 1d6 damage to a creature under your Hex.
  • Patron — The Drowned Widow of Coldmere Bay (Sea Hag)
  • Fishermen along the Jinia coast leave offerings at low tide so she doesn't come looking herself. She was beautiful once, or so the stories insist, right before the sea decided otherwise.
  • Recipe (1st): Murk Brew.
  • Curse (3rd): Once per day, force a creature within 30ft to make a Will save or be wracked by the Drowned Widow's Gaze: its speed is halved and it can't speak (no verbal spells) for the encounter, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns.
  • Physical Change (7th): Your skin turns faintly grey and clammy, and thin gill-like slits appear at your throat.
  • You can breathe underwater and gain a swim speed of 20ft.
  • Once per day, as your action, a creature within 30ft makes a Fortitude save or its lungs seize with phantom water: it falls Prone and loses its next action.
  • Patron — Frostmother Ysolde (Bheur Hag)
  • She comes down from the high passes when the first real cold sets in, and the old villages of the Boldock Wall still leave out food so she passes them by. Some winters she doesn't take the offering. Those are the bad years.
  • Recipe (1st): Hearthfire Broth.
  • Curse (3rd): Once per day, force a creature within 30ft to make a Fortitude save or its speed is halved by bone-deep cold for the encounter, and it takes 1d6 cold damage (2d6 from 13th) at the start of each of its turns; it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on a success.
  • Physical Change (7th): Frost rimes your hair permanently white regardless of true age, and your breath mists even in warm air.
  • Resistance 5 to cold damage.
  • Once per round, when a creature takes damage from your Hex, a spell you cast or your claw, you may add 1d6 cold damage.
  • Patron — Baba Yaga
  • The Grandmother of Witches, older than any coven that claims her, older than most of the borders on any map of Arneyan. Her hut walks on chicken legs somewhere out past the edge of settled land, and it finds the Witches it wants to find — not the other way around.
  • Recipe (1st): Seer's Draught.
  • Curse (3rd): Once per day, set a creature within 30ft an impossible task as a curse (Will save negates) — on a failed save they immediately suffer Disadvantage on all Charisma checks until they attempt the task in good faith (for up to 1 day per Witch level), as if the world itself is waiting on them to finish.
  • Physical Change (7th): Your teeth sharpen slightly and one lock of your hair turns iron-grey no matter your true age.
  • Advantage on Survival checks outside a settlement, and you always know which direction leads to the nearest dwelling, however far.
  • Your natural weapon is a bite.
  • Once per day, out of turn, when struck in melee, the ancient magic in your blood answers unbidden: the attacker takes 2d6 piercing damage (Will save halves).
  • Patron — Mother Loretta
  • Ancient beyond any coven's memory of her arrival, Mother Loretta is said to have written down half the hexes every Witch in Arneyan still uses — usually without anyone crediting her for it.
  • She doesn't take students anymore.
  • She just occasionally shows up to collect what she considers owed.
  • Recipe (1st): Hag's Remedy.
  • Curse (3rd): Once per day, unravel a piece of luck from a creature within 30ft: its next three d20 rolls within the hour are each rolled twice, worst result used (Will negates).
  • Physical Change (7th): Your hair greys prematurely regardless of true age, and small green shoots occasionally bud at your temples.
  • Advantage on Wisdom checks involving herbalism, folk remedies or oral tradition.
  • Once per day, as your action, spit a hex-laced tonic at a creature within 15ft: Fortitude save or Poisoned for the encounter.
  • Patron — The Hollow Bride
  • A Mournas legend — a bride who drowned in the harbour on her wedding night and never stopped waiting at the water's edge. Witches who serve her carry a little of that patience, and a little of that grief.
  • Recipe (1st): Threshold Salt.
  • Curse (3rd): Once per day, bind a creature within 30ft to a single spoken promise (Will save negates) — if they knowingly break it within 24 hours, they take 3d6 cold damage and know exactly why.
  • Physical Change (7th): Your skin is faintly cool to the touch; you cast no reflection and leave no tracks.
  • Advantage on checks to wait, watch or go unnoticed while still.
  • Once per day, as your action, a creature within 30ft that has broken its word to you takes 2d6 cold damage and makes a Fortitude save or gains one level of Exhaustion.
